knowledge_statements.title: Embedded Predictor-Corrector Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mehrotra-type direction construction including scalar HSD complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a positive embedded iterate, set \\(\mu=(x^{\mathsf T}s+\tau\kappa)/(n+1)\\). First solve the full embedded Newton equations with zero target complementarity to obtain the affine direction \\(\Delta z^{\mathrm{aff}}\\). Choose the largest positivity-preserving affine step and compute \\(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\\); set \\(\sigma=(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}/\mu)^3\\). Solve again with target \\(\sigma\mu\\), adding the second-order corrections \\(-\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}\circ\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}\\) and \\(-\Delta\tau^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta\kappa^{\mathrm{aff}}\\) to the two complementarity right-hand sides. Output the combined direction and take a fraction-to-boundary step preserving positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an affine embedded direction, estimate its complementarity reduction, then solve a centered system with vector and scalar second-order corrections.
assumptions_latex: The embedded Newton systems are solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output direction incorporates both predictor progress and corrector centering for \\((x,s)\\) and \\((\tau,\kappa)\\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Neighborhood-preserving predictor–corrector method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating predictor and corrector steps for a homogeneous self-dual LP interior-point method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\le\beta\le1\), define \(\mathcal N(\beta)=\{(x,z)>0:\|XZe-\mu(x,z)e\|\le\beta\mu(x,z)\}\). These neighborhoods increase with \(\beta\), and \(\mathcal N(0)\) consists exactly of points whose components of \(XZe\) are equal. Beginning with a predictor, the method alternates: from \(\mathcal N(1/4)\), compute the direction with \(\delta=0\) and choose \(\theta=\max\{t:(x+t\Delta x,z+t\Delta z)\in\mathcal N(1/2)\}\); from \(\mathcal N(1/2)\), compute the corrector direction with \(\delta=1\) and set \(\theta=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method alternates an uncentered predictor with a full centering corrector. The predictor starts in the one-quarter neighborhood and takes the largest step remaining in the one-half neighborhood; the corrector takes a full step from that larger neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta_{\mathrm{pred}}=0,\quad \theta_{\mathrm{pred}}=\max\{t:(x+t\Delta x,z+t\Delta z)\in\mathcal N(1/2)\};\qquad \delta_{\mathrm{corr}}=1,\quad \theta_{\mathrm{corr}}=1

children.title: HSD Path-Following Methods
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood-based methods following the embedded central trajectory.

knowledge_statements.title: HSD Path-Following Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-step neighborhood method for the embedded central trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a strictly positive embedded point satisfying the chosen HSD affine equations and lying in \\(\mathcal N_2(\theta)=\{z:\lVert (Xs,\tau\kappa)-\mu\mathbf1\rVert_2\le\theta\mu\}\\), where \\(\mu=(x^{\mathsf T}s+\tau\kappa)/(n+1)\\) and \\(0<\theta<1\\). At each iteration choose \\(\mu^+=(1-\delta/\sqrt{n+1})\mu\\), solve the embedded Newton equations targeting \\(x^+\circ s^+=\mu^+e\\) and \\(\tau^+\kappa^+=\mu^+\\), and damp the step if necessary to retain positivity and neighborhood membership. Stop when \\(\mu\\) and the scaled embedded residuals meet the prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a central-path neighborhood while reducing embedded complementarity by a fixed inverse-square-root fraction per Newton iteration.
assumptions_latex: A strictly positive embedded starting point in \\(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\\) is available.
\\(\delta>0\\) is chosen small enough to preserve the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated positive iterates remain in \\(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\\) and decrease \\(\mu\\) geometrically.

children.title: HSD Predictor-Corrector Methods
children.top_down_role: Predictor-corrector variants operating directly on homogeneous self-dual variables.

knowledge_statements.title: HSD Predictor-Corrector Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictor-corrector iteration operating directly on positive HSD variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a positive HSD iterate \\(z=(x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\\), compute an affine-scaling predictor by setting the centering target to zero in all embedded complementarity equations. Determine positivity-preserving affine step lengths and the predicted complementarity \\(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\\). Select \\(\sigma\in[0,1]\\), commonly \\(\sigma=(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}/\mu)^3\\), and compute a corrector containing the affine-product terms for both \\(x\circ s\\) and \\(\tau\kappa\\). Combine the directions, choose primal, dual, and scalar fraction-to-boundary steps, update \\(z\\), and terminate only after residual, complementarity, and HSD status tests pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An HSD predictor-corrector step predicts boundary progress, restores centrality with vector and scalar corrections, then applies status-aware termination tests.
assumptions_latex: Predictor and corrector linear systems admit solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate preserves positivity while updating all primal, dual, and homogeneous variables.

knowledge_statements.title: HSD Polynomial-Complexity Results
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-step iteration bound for an LP HSD embedding with barrier parameter \\(n+1\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a short-step HSD path-following method that remains in a fixed central neighborhood and satisfies \\(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-\delta/\sqrt{n+1})\mu_k\\) for a constant \\(\delta\in(0,1)\\). To obtain \\(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\\), it suffices to perform \\[k=O\!\left(\sqrt{n+1}\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right)\] embedded Newton iterations. Each iteration requires a constant number of solves with an embedded Newton matrix; using scalar elimination, these reduce to solves with the LP core plus rank-at-most-two coupling work. The bound counts exact-arithmetic Newton iterations, not bit complexity or conditioning-dependent numerical refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A short-step HSD method reaches complementarity tolerance epsilon in order square-root-n times the logarithm of the initial-to-final complementarity ratio.
assumptions_latex: Iterates remain in a fixed short-step neighborhood.
The stated uniform complementarity contraction holds.
Embedded Newton systems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(k=O(\sqrt{n+1}\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\\) Newton iterations suffice.

children.title: HSD Termination Status Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Termination families distinguishing optimal recovery, infeasibility certification, and unresolved numerical status.

children.title: Optimal-Solution Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination status supporting recovery of an optimal original-LP solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Solution Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact HSD certificate for a standard-form primal-dual LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal problem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\). If an HSD solution \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) satisfies \(Ax=b\tau\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\tau\), \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y+\kappa=0\), \((x,s,\tau,\kappa)\geq0\), \(\tau>0\), and \(\kappa=0\), terminate with optimal status. The recovered variables \(\hat x=x/\tau\), \(\hat y=y/\tau\), and \(\hat s=s/\tau\) are primal-dual feasible and satisfy \(c^{\mathsf T}\hat x=b^{\mathsf T}\hat y\), hence are optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive recovery scale and zero embedding gap yield feasible recovered primal-dual variables with equal objectives, certifying optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x=x/\tau\) and \((\hat y,\hat s)=(y/\tau,s/\tau)\) are primal-dual optimal.

notation.meaning: variables recovered by division by the positive scale

children.title: Primal-Infeasibility Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination status supported by primal-infeasibility evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas termination certificate extracted from a zero-scale HSD outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal system \(Ax=b\), \(x\geq0\), suppose an HSD outcome has \(\tau=0\) and supplies \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(s\in\mathbb R^n_+\), and \(\kappa>0\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=\kappa\). Terminate with primal-infeasible status. Indeed, the normalized vector \(\bar y=y/\kappa\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}\bar y\leq0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}\bar y=1\). These two relations constitute a directly checkable Farkas certificate that no \(x\geq0\) can satisfy \(Ax=b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-scale HSD vector with nonpositive adjoint image and positive right-hand-side pairing certifies primal infeasibility after normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n_+:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\).

children.title: Dual-Infeasibility Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination status supported by dual-infeasibility evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Infeasibility Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Improving-ray termination certificate for the standard-form primal LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), suppose a zero-scale HSD outcome supplies \(d\in\mathbb R^n_+\) and \(\kappa>0\) satisfying \(Ad=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-\kappa\). Terminate with dual-infeasible status and report \(\bar d=d/\kappa\). Then \(A\bar d=0\), \(\bar d\geq0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar d=-1\), so \(\bar d\) is a primal improving ray. Consequently the dual system \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(s\geq0\), is infeasible. If the primal has a feasible point, its objective is additionally unbounded below along this ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative null-space direction with negative cost certifies dual infeasibility and, when the primal is feasible, primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(y,s):A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\geq0\}=\varnothing\).

children.title: Unresolved-Status Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination without a sufficiently supported solution or certificate status.

knowledge_statements.title: Unresolved-Status Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for termination without a validated HSD status certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix numerical acceptance predicates \(P_{\mathrm{opt}}\), \(P_{\mathrm{pi}}\), and \(P_{\mathrm{di}}\) for, respectively, an approximate optimal solution, a primal-infeasibility certificate, and a dual-infeasibility certificate. If an HSD algorithm reaches an authorized stopping limit while all computed quantities remain finite but none of these predicates holds, its mathematically justified output is unresolved status. In particular, small embedding residual alone does not imply any of the three statuses when both recovery and certificate scales are too small to normalize reliably. Unresolved status makes no claim that the primal or dual problem is feasible, infeasible, bounded, or unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite run ending without any accepted optimality or infeasibility certificate must report unresolved status and make no LP-status claim.
assumptions_latex:
\(
eg P_{\mathrm{opt}}\wedge
eg P_{\mathrm{pi}}\wedge
eg P_{\mathrm{di}}\) at an authorized stopping limit
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{status}=\mathrm{unresolved}\).
review_flags: implementation-dependent stopping predicates require a solver specification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed unresolved status depends on solver-specific stopping limits and acceptance predicates. No source or solver specification establishes that this is the intended HSD termination rule.

children.title: Numerical-Failure Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination caused by unreliable embedded numerical progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Failure Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational failure boundary distinct from a mathematical LP status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An HSD run terminates with numerical-failure status when the next prescribed iterate or status metric cannot be evaluated as a finite real quantity under the implementation's arithmetic model. Qualifying events include a nonfinite iterate, failure of the Newton-system solver to return a direction meeting its declared residual bound, or inability to choose a positive step satisfying the algorithm's neighborhood conditions. Such an event invalidates certificate evaluation; therefore it must not be translated into optimality, primal infeasibility, or dual infeasibility unless an independently checked certificate already satisfies its acceptance predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonfinite arithmetic or failure to compute an admissible direction is a numerical failure, not evidence of any mathematical LP status.
assumptions_latex: \(z_k\) is the current finite HSD iterate
The prescribed numerical subproblem or status metric is not evaluable within its declared bounds
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{status}=\mathrm{numerical\ failure}\), unless an independently verified certificate exists.

children.title: HSD Recovery Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Geometric and numerical regimes in which embedded recovery or certificate interpretation becomes unreliable.

children.title: Trivial Homogeneous-Outcome Boundary
children.top_down_role: Normalization and trajectory regimes associated with the zero embedded solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Trivial Homogeneous-Outcome Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The zero embedded solution carries no recoverable LP information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and consider an HSD embedding with variables \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\tau,\kappa\in\mathbb R\). If its equations and cone constraints are homogeneous in \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\), then \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)=(0,0,0,0,0)\) is feasible for the embedding. This vector cannot certify a status of the original LP: division by \(\tau\) is undefined, and both potential certificate margins \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) and \(-c^{\mathsf T}x\) vanish. Therefore the zero embedded vector is not an acceptable optimality or infeasibility terminal certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The homogeneous zero solution satisfies the embedding but yields neither recovered LP variables nor a nonzero infeasibility margin.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
The embedding equations and cone constraints are homogeneous in \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,0,0,0,0)\) does not certify an original-LP status.

children.title: Vanishing Recovery-Scale Regime
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which conversion to original-LP variables becomes unstable.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Recovery-Scale Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery by division becomes ill-conditioned as the HSD scale vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For an approximate HSD point with \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\tau>0\), define \(r_p=Ax-b\tau\), \(r_d=A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\tau\), and recovered variables \(\hat x=x/\tau\), \(\hat y=y/\tau\), and \(\hat s=s/\tau\). Then \(A\hat x-b=r_p/\tau\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\hat y+\hat s-c=r_d/\tau\). Consequently, if \(\tau_k\downarrow0\) and either corresponding unscaled residual is not \(o(\tau_k)\), that recovered residual does not converge to zero and may diverge. Small absolute embedding residuals alone therefore do not justify accepting a recovered solution in the vanishing-scale regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing by a vanishing recovery scale amplifies primal and dual embedding residuals, so recovery requires those residuals to vanish faster than the scale.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(x_k/\tau_k)-b=r_{p,k}/\tau_k\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}(y_k/\tau_k)+s_k/\tau_k-c=r_{d,k}/\tau_k\), so the recovered residuals need not tend to \(0\).

notation.meaning: variables recovered by division by the positive scale

children.title: Near-Ill-Posed Status Regimes
children.top_down_role: Poorly separated optimality and infeasibility outcomes near the LP ill-posedness boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Ill-Posed Status Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status reliability is bounded by distance to differently classified LP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent LP data by \(d=(A,b,c)\) in a fixed normed data space, and let \(\Sigma\) be the boundary separating data with stable optimal, primal-infeasible, and dual-infeasible statuses. Define \(\delta(d)=\inf_{d'\in\Sigma}\|d-d'\|\). If the combined modeling, rounding, and backward error is bounded only by \(\eta\geq\delta(d)\), the uncertainty ball \(\{d':\|d'-d\|\leq\eta\}\) can meet a different status region. Thus no status inferred solely from computations on perturbed data is robust without a certificate whose residual and margin establish separation stronger than the data uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When data uncertainty reaches the distance to the ill-posedness boundary, nearby LPs may have different statuses, so classification is not robust.
assumptions_latex: LP data use a fixed norm \(\|\cdot\|\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The uncertainty ball of radius \(\eta\) is not guaranteed to lie in one LP-status region.

notation.meaning: distance from the data to that boundary

review_flags: requires an authoritative condition-number treatment defining the chosen status boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An authoritative condition-number source is required to define the data space, status regions, and ill-posedness set. At equality \(\eta=\delta(d)\), intersection with the boundary also requires attainment or closure assumptions, and intersection with a different open status region is not automatic.

children.title: Finite-Precision Status Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Competing approximate recovery and infeasibility indicators.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Status Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-error balls can support competing approximate status indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d=(A,b,c)\) be stored LP data and let \(\mathcal B_\eta(d)=\{d':\|d'-d\|\leq\eta\}\) describe admissible backward error. Finite-precision status is ambiguous whenever there exist \(d_1,d_2\in\mathcal B_\eta(d)\) having different exact statuses and the computed HSD quantities satisfy the implementation's residual tests for indicators associated with both statuses. In this case residual magnitudes alone do not select a logically unique status. The solver must report ambiguity or unresolved status unless interval verification, directed rounding, or a stricter certificate proves that one status holds for the intended data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the backward-error ball contains LPs of different statuses and competing indicators pass, finite-precision computation cannot select a unique status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A unique status for \(d\) is not certified by the competing approximate indicators.

children.title: Certificate Normalization
children.top_down_role: Normalization choices used to present embedded certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical unit-margin forms of homogeneous LP infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). A primal-infeasibility ray \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y\leq0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y>0\) is positively homogeneous. Its unit-margin representative is \(\bar y=y/(b^{\mathsf T}y)\), for which \(A^{\mathsf T}\bar y\leq0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}\bar y=1\). Likewise, a dual-infeasibility ray \(x\in\mathbb R^n_+\) satisfying \(Ax=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}x<0\) has representative \(\bar x=x/(-c^{\mathsf T}x)\), for which \(A\bar x=0\), \(\bar x\geq0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar x=-1\). Positive rescaling preserves the certified status whenever the normalizing denominator is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide each homogeneous infeasibility ray by its strict certificate margin to obtain a unit-margin certificate while preserving its cone and null-space relations.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(y\in\mathbb R^m,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\leq0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y>0\) for primal infeasibility
\(x\in\mathbb R^n_+,\ Ax=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}x<0\) for dual infeasibility
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^{\mathsf T}\bar y=1\) or \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar x=-1\), with the corresponding cone and null-space relations preserved.

children.title: Scale-Induced Quality Loss
children.top_down_role: Certificate degradation associated with extreme or unsuitable scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Induced Quality Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small certificate margins amplify residuals during normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For an approximate primal-infeasibility ray \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(\alpha=b^{\mathsf T}y>0\) and \(e=(A^{\mathsf T}y)_+\), where the positive part is componentwise. With \(\bar y=y/\alpha\), one has \((A^{\mathsf T}\bar y)_+=e/\alpha\) and therefore \(\|(A^{\mathsf T}\bar y)_+\|=\|e\|/\alpha\). Similarly, for an approximate dual-infeasibility ray \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(\beta=-c^{\mathsf T}x>0\), \(q=Ax\), and \(\bar x=x/\beta\); then \(A\bar x=q/\beta\) and \(\|A\bar x\|=\|q\|/\beta\). Thus small unnormalized residuals need not yield high-quality normalized certificates when their strict margins are small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalization divides certificate residuals by the strict margin, so a small margin can amplify small absolute errors into large normalized violations.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|(A^{\mathsf T}(y/\alpha))_+\|=\|e\|/\alpha\) and \(\|A(x/\beta)\|=\|q\|/\beta\).

children.title: Directional Accuracy Loss
children.top_down_role: Loss of certificate reliability caused by inaccurate embedded directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Accuracy Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate validity depends on direction, not merely vector magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_\star\) be a normalized primal-infeasibility certificate with \(b^{\mathsf T}y_\star=1\) and componentwise slack \(-A^{\mathsf T}y_\star\geq\gamma\mathbf1\) for some \(\gamma>0\). For a directional perturbation \(h\), the candidate \(y=y_\star+h\) retains the adjoint inequality whenever \(\|A^{\mathsf T}h\|_\infty\leq\gamma\), and retains a positive certificate margin whenever \(|b^{\mathsf T}h|<1\). If either bound fails, an arbitrarily small relative error measured in an unsuitable scaled norm may destroy certificate validity. Thus certificate quality requires directional residual and margin checks after normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturbations preserve a strict infeasibility certificate only while their adjoint and margin effects remain below the certificate's directional margins.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\|A^{\mathsf T}h\|_\infty\leq\gamma\) and \(|b^{\mathsf T}h|<1\), then \(A^{\mathsf T}y\leq0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y>0\).
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports the directional perturbation bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed sufficient perturbation bounds are algebraically plausible, but no source supports the directional-accuracy formulation. children.title: Interpretability Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where recovered certificate information cannot support a stable interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpretability Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for interpreting approximate homogeneous self-dual embedding outputs as original-LP solutions or certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an approximate homogeneous self-dual output contain scaling variables \(\tau\ge 0\) and \(\kappa\ge 0\). Recovery of a finite primal-dual point by division through \(\tau\) is interpretable only when \(\tau>0\) and the scaled residuals divided by \(\tau\) satisfy the original-model tolerances. An infeasibility or unboundedness interpretation based on division through \(\kappa\) is reliable only when \(\kappa>0\), the associated normalized direction satisfies the required sign and homogeneous equations, and its separating scalar is bounded away from zero. If both scales are numerically negligible, or normalization amplifies residuals beyond tolerance, the embedding output has no justified original-model interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An HSD output is uninterpretable when its normalizing scale is negligible, its normalized residuals are too large, or the proposed direction lacks the required separating sign.
assumptions_latex: The embedding variables and residual equations use a fixed homogeneous self-dual LP convention.
Original-model accuracy tolerances are specified before recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau\approx0\) and \(\kappa\approx0\), or excessive residual amplification under normalization, precludes a justified solution or certificate classification.

children.title: Standard-Form Conversion Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form Conversion Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence interface from bounded, ranged general-form LP constraints to equality standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(l\le Ax\le u\) and \(\ell\le x\le v\), with infinite bounds omitted. Introduce one nonnegative slack for each finite one-sided inequality, split every free variable as \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\), translate each finitely lower-bounded variable by \(x_j=\ell_j+z_j\), and represent each finite upper bound by a nonnegative complementary slack. After collecting constants, these substitutions produce \(\min\{\bar c^{\mathsf T}z+\gamma:\bar A z=\bar b,\ z\ge0\}\). The conversion interface must retain the affine reconstruction \(x=Tz+d\) and objective offset \(\gamma\), so feasible points and objective values correspond in both directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack variables, variable splitting, and bound shifts convert a general LP to equality standard form while an affine map and objective offset preserve interpretation.
assumptions_latex: All coefficients and finite bounds are real.
Each introduced slack or split component is constrained nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The converted model has form \(\bar A z=\bar b\), \(z\ge0\), with reconstruction \(x=Tz+d\) and objective identity \(c^{\mathsf T}x=\bar c^{\mathsf T}z+\gamma\).

children.title: Presolve Transformation Ledger
children.top_down_role: Recorded correspondence between original-model entities and presolved entities.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Transformation Ledger
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composable ledger required to reverse exact presolve transformations and recover original-model objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presolve ledger is an ordered sequence \(\mathcal L=(R_1,\ldots,R_k)\) accompanying reduced LP data. Each record \(R_i\) specifies a transformation of primal variables, constraints, objective constants, and dual quantities, together with a partial inverse \(R_i^{-1}\) on the transformation's valid image. If presolve maps the original model \(P_0\) successively to \(P_k\), postsolve applies \(R_1^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ R_k^{-1}\) to a reduced solution or certificate, in reverse execution order. Exact recoverability requires every eliminated value, substitution coefficient, scaling factor, bound change, row operation, and objective offset needed by these inverses to be retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve ledger records reversible transformations and applies their inverses in reverse order to reconstruct original solutions, certificates, and objective values.
assumptions_latex: Each presolve step has a specified inverse on the reduced objects it can validly receive.
No information required by an inverse is discarded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every recoverable object \(q_0\), postsolve satisfies \(q_0=(R_1^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ R_k^{-1})(q_k)\).

notation.meaning: LP after the first i presolve transformations
solution or certificate object at stage i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but no source supports the proposed ledger abstraction or its required fields. The composition notation also needs an explicit convention confirming that the displayed inverse composition is applied in reverse execution order.

children.title: Reduced-System Rank Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between presolve reductions and the rank structure of the solved system.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-System Rank Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank relation for exact row and column eliminations used by LP presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose invertible row and column transformations reduce an equality matrix to \(UAV=\begin{bmatrix}A_r&B\\0&C\end{bmatrix}\), where \(C\) is a nonsingular square block corresponding to variables and equations eliminated by exact substitution. Then \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}(A_r)+\dim(C)\). Consequently, the reduced matrix \(A_r\) has full row rank exactly when the non-eliminated row space is independent after accounting for the pivot block. If a purported elimination uses a singular or numerically unresolved pivot block, this rank correspondence and unique recovery of the eliminated variables are not justified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a nonsingular pivot block subtracts its dimension from matrix rank; singular or unresolved pivots invalidate the correspondence and unique recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}(A_r)+\dim(C)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind and exact block-rank formula are mathematically appropriate under the stated invertibility assumptions, but the record has no inspectable source locator. The numerical-pivot failure claim likewise requires sourced qualification.

children.title: Eliminated-Variable Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery interface for variables removed during presolve.

knowledge_statements.title: Eliminated-Variable Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse-substitution algorithm for variables removed by exact affine presolve eliminations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a reduced solution \(z\) and a presolve ledger whose eliminations, in forward order, have forms \(x_{j_i}=\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x_{S_i}\). Initialize the retained components of \(x\) from \(z\). Traverse the eliminations in reverse order; at step \(i\), after all components indexed by \(S_i\) are available, set \(x_{j_i}:=\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x_{S_i}\). Reverse stored translations, sign changes, and scalings afterward in their recorded order. Output \(x\) only if every reconstructed component satisfies its original bounds and the original residual test; otherwise report postsolve recovery failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover eliminated variables by reversing recorded affine substitutions, then accept the reconstructed point only after original bounds and residuals are checked.
assumptions_latex: Every elimination is an exact affine substitution recorded in the ledger.
The dependency order is acyclic and retained variables are supplied by the reduced solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an original-space vector \(x\) satisfying all recorded substitution identities, or an explicit recovery-failure status.

notation.meaning: indices needed to reconstruct eliminated component i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but no source supports the recovery procedure. The instruction to reverse translations, sign changes, and scalings afterward in their recorded order is ambiguous and may conflict with the required reverse order of a general transformation ledger.

children.title: Presolve-Induced Certificate Effects
children.top_down_role: Effects of presolve transformations on certificate interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve-Induced Certificate Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of exact presolve maps on LP infeasibility certificates and improving rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let presolve map original primal variables by \(x=Tz+d\) and transform equality rows by an invertible matrix \(M\), while recording every eliminated constraint and bound. A reduced feasible solution maps forward through \(Tz+d\), but a reduced dual certificate must be pulled back through the adjoint row and substitution maps, with eliminated-row multipliers restored. Likewise, a reduced recession direction \(r\\) maps to \(Tr\), without the translation \(d\). Certificate validity is preserved only when the reconstructed object satisfies the original homogeneous equations, sign restrictions, and a strict separating inequality; objective offsets do not enter homogeneous rays but can affect finite objective-value recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve maps points affinely, rays linearly, and dual certificates through adjoint transformations; omitted eliminated-row data can destroy certificate recovery.
assumptions_latex: Presolve transformations are exact and their inverse or adjoint recovery data are retained.
Certificates are checked against the original LP after reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid postsolve certificates must satisfy the original equations, sign conditions, and strict separation test after the appropriate pullback.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits, but the general adjoint pullback and restoration of eliminated multipliers are convention-dependent and unsupported. children.title: Original-Model Solution Mapping

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Model Solution Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Postsolve representation of primal-dual solutions after affine variable and invertible row transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original equality-form primal be \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\\ x\ge0\}\), and suppose preprocessing uses \(x=Tz+d\) together with invertible row transformations and recorded eliminations to obtain a reduced primal-dual pair. Define the postsolve map by reversing all transformations in ledger order, reconstructing \(x\), the original dual multiplier \(y\), and slack \(s=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\). A reduced candidate represents an original-model solution only if \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(s\ge0\), and its recovered objective includes every stored constant offset. Under exact recovery, complementary solutions satisfy \(x^{\mathsf T}s=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve reverses preprocessing and accepts a mapped solution only when original primal feasibility, dual feasibility, objective offsets, and complementarity are restored.
assumptions_latex: All preprocessing transformations and eliminated quantities are recorded exactly.
The reduced candidate lies in the domain of every inverse transformation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered \((x,y,s)\) is an original primal-dual solution precisely when the original feasibility and complementarity relations hold.

notation.meaning: original primal vector, dual multiplier, and dual slack

children.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Mapping

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Postsolve mapping and verification of a Farkas certificate for equality-form primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the original system \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), a primal-infeasibility certificate is a vector \(y\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\). Given a reduced certificate \(\hat y\), postsolve must reverse every row operation by the corresponding adjoint map and restore multipliers for eliminated rows and bounds, producing \(y=Q(\hat y)\). The reduced certificate transfers to the original model only if direct evaluation with original data confirms both displayed inequalities. Positive rescaling preserves validity, whereas a sign reversal does not. Failure of either original-data test rejects the mapped certificate regardless of reduced-system status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced infeasibility certificate is valid after postsolve only if its pulled-back multiplier satisfies the original Farkas sign and strict-separation inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The original primal feasibility system is \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\).
The postsolve pullback includes all eliminated-row and bound multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}Q(\hat y)\ge0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}Q(\hat y)<0\) certify infeasibility of the original system.

children.title: Unbounded-Ray Mapping

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Ray Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Postsolve mapping and original-data verification of a primal improving recession ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), a primal unboundedness ray is a nonzero vector \(r\) satisfying \(Ar=0\), \(r\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}r<0\), provided at least one primal feasible point exists. If presolve uses the affine solution map \(x=Tz+d\), a reduced ray \(\hat r\) maps homogeneously as \(r=T\hat r\); the translation \(d\) is omitted. Postsolve accepts the ray only after checking the three ray conditions with original data. Under these conditions, every feasible \(x_0\) generates feasible points \(x_0+tr\) whose objectives tend to \(-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced improving ray maps through the linear part of postsolve and certifies unboundedness only after original homogeneous and objective tests pass.
assumptions_latex: The original minimization LP has a feasible point.
The linear part \(T\) of the presolve reconstruction is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(r=T\hat r\neq0\), \(Ar=0\), \(r\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}r<0\), then the original LP is unbounded below.

children.title: Transformation-Reversal Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes limiting reliable reversal of model transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation-Reversal Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which reduced solutions or certificates cannot be validly reconstructed in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Postsolve reversal fails if any recorded inverse is undefined at the reduced output, if a required pivot or scale is zero, if eliminated-variable dependencies are cyclic or incomplete, or if finite-precision reversal produces violations beyond original-model tolerances. It also fails for certificates when a transformation preserves feasible points but lacks the adjoint data needed to restore eliminated multipliers. Formally, for ledger map \(R=R_k\circ\cdots\circ R_1\), reconstruction is justified only on \(\operatorname{dom}(R^{-1})\), with all intermediate inverse states defined and the final object passing original equations, signs, bounds, and strict-separation tests. Reduced-system acceptance alone is insufficient outside this domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve is invalid when an inverse is undefined, recovery data are missing, numerical reversal exceeds tolerance, or the final object fails original-model checks.
assumptions_latex: A transformation ledger and reduced output are supplied.
Original-model feasibility and certificate tolerances are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the reduced output is outside \(\operatorname{dom}(R^{-1})\) or fails direct original-data validation, no original-model solution or certificate is established.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but no source supports the claimed exhaustive failure conditions, partial-inverse formulation, or certificate-adjoint requirements. Numerical failure also depends on an explicit solver tolerance and scaling policy.

children.title: Scaled Optimality Accuracy Measures
children.top_down_role: Accuracy families for primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity.

children.title: Scaled Primal-Residual Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Scaled accuracy reporting for primal feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Primal-Residual Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless normwise accuracy measure for the equality residual of a standard-form primal candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the standard-form primal constraints \(Ax=b\), define the scaled primal-residual accuracy of a candidate \(x\) by
\[\eta_p(x):=\frac{\|Ax-b\|}{1+\|A\|\,\|x\|+\|b\|}.\]
The vector norm and its induced matrix norm must be fixed consistently. A solver declares primal-residual accuracy at tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\ge0\) when \(\eta_p(x)\le\varepsilon_p\). This measure assesses the equality equations only; nonnegativity or bound violations require separate scaled tests. The additive constant prevents division by zero and fixes the convention for data near the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled primal accuracy divides the equality residual norm by a data-and-solution scale and compares the resulting dimensionless quantity with a chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is induced by the selected vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal equations meet tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\) exactly when \(\eta_p(x)\le\varepsilon_p\).

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the exact denominator is a convention rather than a universal LP residual definition. Wright p. 8 does not demonstrably support this normalization, so a source stating the precise scaled-residual formula is required.

children.title: Scaled Dual-Residual Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Scaled accuracy reporting for dual feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Dual-Residual Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless normwise accuracy measure for the dual stationarity equation in standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the dual equations \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), define the scaled dual-residual accuracy of a candidate \((y,s)\) by
\[\eta_d(y,s):=\frac{\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|}{1+\|A\|\,\|y\|+\|s\|+\|c\|}.\]
The vector norm and corresponding induced matrix norm must be fixed consistently. A solver declares dual-residual accuracy at tolerance \(\varepsilon_d\ge0\) when \(\eta_d(y,s)\le\varepsilon_d\). This equation measure does not itself enforce the sign condition \(s\ge0\); negative dual slack requires a separate scaled violation test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled dual accuracy normalizes the stationarity residual by the magnitudes of the data and dual variables, with slack-sign feasibility tested separately.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is induced by the selected vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual stationarity meets tolerance \(\varepsilon_d\) exactly when \(\eta_d(y,s)\le\varepsilon_d\).

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the exact normalization is unsupported. For general induced norms, the stationarity bound naturally involves the operator norm of A transpose between the selected spaces; writing norm A requires additional assumptions such as compatible Euclidean norms. A precise sourced convention is required.

children.title: Scaled Complementarity-Gap Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Scaled accuracy reporting for complementarity or objective-gap measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Complementarity-Gap Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative complementarity measure for a primal-dual iterate in standard-form linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal problem \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge 0\}\), define the scaled complementarity-gap measure of \((x,y,s)\) by \[\eta_g(x,y,s):=\frac{|c^Tx-b^Ty|}{1+|c^Tx|+|b^Ty|}.\] The iterate has scaled complementarity-gap accuracy \(\varepsilon_g\ge 0\) exactly when \(\eta_g(x,y,s)\le\varepsilon_g\). If both affine equations hold, then \(c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts\), so the numerator equals the complementarity gap whenever \(x,s\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative objective gap is the absolute primal-dual objective difference divided by one plus both objective magnitudes; accuracy requires this measure not to exceed its tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_g(x,y,s)\le\varepsilon_g\).

children.title: Cross-Measure Tolerance Balance
children.top_down_role: Coordination of tolerances across multiple reported accuracy measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Measure Tolerance Balance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint acceptance condition preventing one residual class from compensating for another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\eta_p,\eta_d,\eta_g\ge0\) be the scaled primal-residual, dual-residual, and complementarity-gap measures of one solver iterate, with positive tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\). The cross-measure tolerance-balance condition is \[\rho:=\max\left\{\frac{\eta_p}{\varepsilon_p},\frac{\eta_d}{\varepsilon_d},\frac{\eta_g}{\varepsilon_g}\right\}\le1.\] Thus every measure must meet its own tolerance; a small value of one measure cannot offset a violation by another. When a single tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is used, this reduces to \(\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d,\eta_g\}\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint accuracy holds only when each scaled residual or gap meets its assigned tolerance, equivalently when the largest tolerance-normalized measure is at most one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\le1\iff \eta_p\le\varepsilon_p,\ \eta_d\le\varepsilon_d,\ \eta_g\le\varepsilon_g\).

notation.meaning: scaled primal, dual, and gap error measures

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), an iterate \((x,y,s)\) receives optimal-solution status at tolerances \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g)\) when \(x\ge0\), \(s\ge0\), and its prescribed scaled measures satisfy \[\eta_p(x)\le\varepsilon_p,\qquad \eta_d(y,s)\le\varepsilon_d,\qquad \eta_g(x,y,s)\le\varepsilon_g.\] Exact optimal status is the zero-tolerance case. For positive tolerances this status asserts only approximate feasibility and approximate zero duality gap under the declared scaling conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal status requires nonnegative primal and dual slacks plus simultaneous satisfaction of the scaled primal, dual, and objective-gap tolerances.

children.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Status
children.top_down_role: Status families distinguishing primal and dual infeasibility outcomes and certificate quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Farkas-ray statuses for standard-form primal and dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(D=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), primal-infeasibility status is certified by \(u\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \[A^Tu\ge0,\qquad b^Tu<0.\] Dual-infeasibility status is certified by \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \[Ad=0,\qquad d\ge0,\qquad c^Td<0.\] The first system contradicts primal feasibility; the second is a primal feasible recession direction with strictly decreasing objective. Approximate certificate status must additionally declare normalization and residual tolerances and must not be identified with either exact status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal infeasibility uses a Farkas multiplier; dual infeasibility uses a nonnegative primal recession direction of strictly negative cost. Approximate variants require explicit normalization and tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(u\) certifies infeasibility of \(P\), while the displayed \(d\) certifies infeasibility of \(D\).

children.title: Iteration-Limit Status
children.top_down_role: Unresolved status caused by exhaustion of an iteration allowance.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration-Limit Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination caused solely by exhaustion of the permitted iteration budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an equation-system solver produce iterates \(z^0,z^1,\ldots\), let \(K\in\mathbb N\) be its iteration budget, and let \(T(z)\) denote the disjunction of all conclusive optimality and infeasibility acceptance tests. Iteration-limit status is returned precisely when \[k=K,\qquad T(z^j)=\mathrm{false}\ \text{for every }0\le j\le K,\] and no earlier numerical-breakdown condition terminated the run. The status records budget exhaustion only: it implies neither feasibility nor infeasibility and does not convert the last iterate into a mathematical certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration-limit status means the allowed iterations were exhausted before any conclusive acceptance test or earlier breakdown occurred; it makes no claim about the linear program.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb N\) is fixed before or during the run by the solver policy.
Conclusive tests and numerical-breakdown precedence are specified by the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run terminates with iteration-limit status and no optimality or infeasibility conclusion.

children.title: Numerical-Breakdown Status
children.top_down_role: Failure status caused by unreliable numerical linear algebra or iterate updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Breakdown Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconclusive termination when finite-precision arithmetic invalidates a required solver operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k\) be a finite-precision solver state and let \(U_k(z^k)\) be the next prescribed update. Numerical-breakdown status is returned when no conclusive status has been accepted and \(U_k\) cannot be validly completed because a required quantity is nonfinite, a required linear-system solve fails its declared residual test, or a required positivity or domain condition cannot be maintained after the permitted safeguards. Formally, with \(V_k\) the update-validity predicate, \[T(z^k)=\mathrm{false},\qquad V_k(z^k)=\mathrm{false}.\] This computational status is not an optimality or infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical breakdown means a required finite-precision update fails its declared validity checks before any conclusive status is accepted; it proves nothing about the underlying problem.
assumptions_latex: The implementation declares finite-value, linear-solve, and domain-validity tests.
Permitted regularization, refinement, and step safeguards have been exhausted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run terminates nonconclusively because \(V_k(z^k)=\mathrm{false}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: failed finite-precision validity checks define conventional numerical-breakdown termination

children.title: Ambiguous-Certificate Status
children.top_down_role: Unresolved status caused by insufficiently reliable certificate evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous-Certificate Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination when competing approximate certificate tests pass without a unique defensible classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_O(z)\), \(C_P(z)\), and \(C_D(z)\) be the declared acceptance predicates for approximate optimality, primal infeasibility, and dual infeasibility at a recovered state \(z\). Ambiguous-certificate status applies when the accepted set \[S(z):=\{q\in\{O,P,D\}:C_q(z)=\mathrm{true}\}\] has cardinality \(|S(z)|\ge2\), or when a certificate passes its residual test but fails the interface's required sign, normalization, or separation test. No member of \(S(z)\) may then be reported as a unique conclusive status without an explicit tie-breaking or strengthened verification rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate is ambiguous when incompatible status tests pass together, or when residual accuracy passes but required sign, normalization, or separation checks do not.
assumptions_latex: All status predicates use the same recovered state and declared tolerances.
The interface treats optimality, primal infeasibility, and dual infeasibility as mutually exclusive conclusive labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No unique label in \(\{O,P,D\}\) is certified by the current tests.

children.title: Indeterminate Recovery Status
children.top_down_role: Unresolved status caused by unreliable solution recovery or postsolve interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Indeterminate Recovery Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding termination without a stable recovery denominator or an accepted infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an embedding solver terminates with state \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s,\bar\tau,\bar\kappa)\), where recovery of an original primal-dual candidate requires division by \(\bar\tau\). Given a recovery threshold \(\tau_{\min}>0\), indeterminate recovery status applies when \[0\le\bar\tau<\tau_{\min}\] and neither the declared primal-infeasibility nor dual-infeasibility certificate test passes. Because division by such \(\bar\tau\) is disallowed or numerically unreliable, the interface returns no recovered solution. This status makes no claim that the original linear program is feasible, infeasible, bounded, or unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery is indeterminate when the embedding scale is too small for reliable dehomogenization and no accepted infeasibility certificate is available.
assumptions_latex: Original variables are recovered by \((x,y,s)=(\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)/\bar\tau\).
\(\tau_{\min}>0\) and the infeasibility-certificate tests are declared by the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No original-space solution or infeasibility classification is returned.
